title: Vaccines during pregnancy
what: Some vaccines during pregnancy protect both mother and baby in the first months of life. Others must not be given. Your doctor will advise.
why: A flu vaccine is usually advised, and in many countries whooping cough in the second half of pregnancy. Sometimes others, if needed.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: What vaccines you had before pregnancy
If you are ill now or have a fever

prepare.title: Talk it through
prepare.text: Discuss vaccines with the doctor who looks after your pregnancy. They will choose which and when.

prepare.title: Live vaccines
prepare.text: Some vaccines, such as measles and chickenpox, are not given in pregnancy. It is best to have them before.

steps: The doctor asks how far along you are and how you feel
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes a sore arm for 1 to 2 days, or tiredness
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
Record the vaccine in your pregnancy record
Tell your doctor how you felt at the next visit
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services
Bleeding, pain low in the belly, or your baby has stopped moving: call emergency services

faq.q: Could the vaccine harm my baby?
faq.a: Vaccines advised in pregnancy are well studied. Protective antibodies pass to your baby.

faq.q: What if I got a live vaccine by accident?
faq.a: Do not panic, and tell your doctor. Usually it is not a cause for alarm. Your doctor will explain.

reminders.text: Vaccine tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record and vaccination certificate.
